jobs.title: Technology Project Manager (Full Stack)
jobs.description: Sole technical owner for the production of two national TV competition shows (Pukllaspa Yachay and Que Gane el Mejor): 5 years of live broadcasts with zero on-air failures. Built and operated live 20+ interactive games, which I moved from Unity to the web with Next.js and deployed on AWS. Rebuilt the production's internal file system with Next.js, NestJS and PostgreSQL on AWS, with Docker and CI/CD, and integrated a local LLM into the games' data collector.

queGane.title: Que Gane el Mejor
queGane.subtitle: The live interactive games of a school competition show on TV Perú, and the production systems behind them.
about: “Que Gane el Mejor” is a TV Perú competition show that pits two schools against each other per episode, with teams of seven high-school seniors competing in knowledge games.
It airs live, with games like “Personajes” and “Mi libro favorito”, and grand finals bringing together hundreds of students from schools across the country.

system.label: Real-time:
system.text: the on-screen games, scores and show flow, live

system.label: Operated from the switcher:
system.text: I operated it myself during the broadcast

system.label: No margin for error:
system.text: any failure had to be resolved within seconds, live on air

system.label: Sole technical owner:
system.text: development, infrastructure and operation were on me

role.title: Games from Unity to the web
role.body: When the show started I moved the interactive games from Unity to the web: first with Next.js alone, then with the full stack deployed on AWS. I operated them myself from the switcher during every broadcast.

role.title: The production's internal file system
role.body: I maintained and then rebuilt the system where production stores its recordings, images and documents: from React, Express and MySQL on a local PC to Next.js, NestJS, TypeScript and PostgreSQL on AWS (EC2 and S3), with Docker and CI/CD with GitHub Actions. Along the way I fixed a SQL injection flaw and plain-text password storage.

role.title: Data collector with a local LLM
role.body: I built the games' data collector. From mid-2025 I integrated a local LLM into it (Qwen 2.5 on Ollama, dockerized): given a topic, the model returned JSON in a defined format, which the system turned into game questions ready for the teacher's review. It also corrected spelling and reduced the repetitive manual work of loading content.

role.title: Live audience voting
role.body: I developed a QR-based voting system for viewers to back a school, with anti-abuse protection to prevent multiple votes. It was later handed over to TV Perú's engineering team.

impact.title: Zero on-air failures
impact.desc: Live broadcasts on national television, with zero on-air failures.

impact.title: From a local PC to the cloud
impact.desc: The production's file system stopped depending on a single machine and moved to AWS, with automated deployment.

impact.title: National reach
impact.desc: Over 600 students from 28 schools across different regions of Peru.

impact.title: Sole technical owner
impact.desc: Development, infrastructure and live operation by a single person.

pukllaspa.title: Pukllaspa Yachay
pukllaspa.subtitle: Where it all started: a daily TV Perú competition show in Quechua, with 20+ interactive games built in Unity and operated live.
about: Pukllaspa Yachay (“Learning by Playing”) was a TV Perú competition show to promote learning the Quechua language, with a daily contest between three participants.
It aired live for more than two years. It was the first program I built the games for, and the starting point of everything that came after.

system.label: Real-time:
system.text: control of the show flow, rounds and scores live

system.label: Daily data:
system.text: each broadcast required new questions, images and per-game structures

system.label: No margin for error:
system.text: any failure had to be resolved within seconds, live on air

role.title: Real-time interactive games
role.body: I developed in Unity/C# the software that controls the live show: participant management, rounds, and 20+ interactive on-screen games, each with its own scoring system, operated by me during the broadcast.

role.title: Daily data collector
role.body: Since the show aired daily, I built a separate system to load each broadcast's data — questions, images and different structures per game — so production could prepare the day's content without touching the game software.

role.title: Live reliability
role.body: On a live show any error had to be resolved within seconds. The games ran full seasons with zero on-air failures.

role.title: Integration with production
role.body: The software integrated with TV Perú's production to control on-screen graphics, scores and transitions between show segments.

impact.title: Live national broadcast
impact.desc: Program aired daily on TV Perú for more than two years.

impact.title: Failure-free operation
impact.desc: The games ran full seasons live, with zero on-air failures.

impact.title: Foundation for what followed
impact.desc: The games I built here were the starting point of the ones I later moved to the web for “Que Gane el Mejor”.

impact.title: Cultural preservation
impact.desc: A contribution to promoting and teaching the Quechua language in Peru.
